1	# Executable requirements — the framework standard
2	
3	The concrete conventions for running a numbered spec as tests. The judgment layer — doc-first
4	red-by-default, owner-owned expecteds, honest-gap tracking — is the
5	[spec-driven-product](../spec-driven-product/RULES.md) playbook; this pack is the mechanics that
6	implement it, so a new project or a new stack adopts the framework by convention instead of
7	re-deriving it. Worked implementations: GoogleCalendarEventCreator (origin; extension/jsdom
8	rendering), TLDR (adds a cross-tier `server` kind), ShoutsAndWhispers (Flutter port; first `saga`
9	kind).
10	
11	## 1. The layout is the contract
12	
13	- Everything lives under **`dev/requirements/`**: `requirements.md` (the numbered prose spec),
14	  one **top-level folder per kind**, `shared/` for cross-kind infra, and the runners/gates. The
15	  spec file's path is the framework's structural fingerprint — this pack activates on it.
16	- **A requirement line** starts (optionally after a list dash) with a backtick-wrapped dotted
17	  number: `` `4.2` ``. A **leaf** is an id with no finer-numbered child. Parse with one shared
18	  regex (`` ^\s*(?:-\s+)?`(\d+(?:\.\d+)+)` ``) so specs stay drop-in compatible across projects.
19	- **The line is a scannable one-liner; expanded detail collapses.** A leaf in `requirements.md`
20	  reads as a single line the owner skims down the numbered spine on GitHub. Any expansion —
21	  rationale, acceptance notes, edge cases, the owner-verification recipe — lives inside a
22	  collapsed `<details>` block under the line, hidden until the owner expands it. The doc reviews
23	  as a clean spec, not walls of prose; the depth is one click away when wanted, invisible when
24	  not.
25	- **The folder is the kind.** A case's kind is the directory it lives in; the case declares no
26	  kind field. Cases are
27	  `<kind>/cases/<slug>.<leaf-id>.case.<ext>`: a stable feature slug (so retitling a spec section
28	  never forces renames), then the dotted leaf id.
29	- **Artifact expecteds live beside their case** (`<slug>.<id>.png`, `expected/<name>.json`);
30	  failure artifacts (actual/diff renders) go to a gitignored dir, never beside the goldens.
31	- Where the language discovers cases dynamically (Node `require`), the registry walks the
32	  folders; where it cannot (Dart/Flutter), each kind keeps a hand-written `manifest` and **the
33	  gate enforces manifest ⇄ disk equality** — an unregistered case file never runs, so unregistered
34	  must be red.
35	
36	## 2. What the coverage gate checks
37	
38	The bijection gate is one committed test. It must fail on every one of: a leaf no case claims
39	(doc-first red-by-default); a case claiming a non-existent leaf; two cases claiming one leaf; a misnamed case file; a kind directory absent from the registry (or a
40	registered kind with no directory); a manifest out of sync with disk (where manifests exist); an
41	image found in a coded kind's folder (a screenshot cannot verify a gesture or a pure rule); a
42	stray golden no case or step accounts for. Every rule iterates the registry — adding a kind never
43	edits the gate.
44	
45	The gate checks repo state; an interactive feature run also has an *ordering*: after the
46	owner's feature-classified comment, an independent commit updating the spec (no code alongside)
47	precedes the first code commit on the branch. The spec's path defaults to the canonical
48	`dev/requirements/requirements.md`; a project whose spec lives elsewhere (a non-canonical
49	layout, or the pack pulled in via a `requires` from `spec-driven-product`) names it on the pack
50	entry as `config.spec`.
51	
52	## 3. The kind vocabulary
53	
54	Two forces pick a leaf's kind: what can **honestly observe** the assertion, and what gives the
55	**owner the simplest verification**. Prefer the kind whose expected is a **visual the owner checks
56	by sight** — a surface snapshot or a saga storyboard — and whose per-leaf test body is minimal:
57	drive to the state, capture, done, with the golden as the assertion rather than hand-written
58	expectations. Push as many requirements as can honestly be seen onto that visual path — the more
59	of the spec an owner verifies by *looking*, the more of it they actually review. Reserve the coded
60	kinds (behavior, logic) for what an image genuinely cannot see: a gesture's outgoing request, a
61	pure rule. Route each leaf to the kind that can actually see what it asserts:
62	
63	- **surface snapshot** (`popup`, `icon`, `screen`, …): a rendered resting state, pixel-exact
64	  against a committed golden. One golden per leaf, even when several leaves render the same state
65	  — the bijection stays strict.
66	- **behavior**: a driven gesture and its outgoing request/consequence, asserted in code against
67	  the fakes' recordings. No images allowed in the folder.
68	- **logic**: a pure product rule, a coded `verify()` importing shipped code.
69	- **saga** (§4): a multi-step story as a golden storyboard.
70	- **per-project kinds** where the product's value is breadth or crosses tiers: a per-target
71	  `extractor`/`support` kind (one case per supported external target, proven on committed real
72	  samples), a `server` kind (the boundary's half of a two-tier rule, against the real handler).
73	- **heavy/e2e singleton**: "the product loads in the real environment" — one case, its own lane,
74	  never in the default loop.
75	
76	## 4. Sagas: stories as storyboards
77	
78	Single frames prove states; **sagas prove transitions and causality** — what arriving, acting, or
79	time passing *changes*. Use a saga when the requirement is the story ("a message sent before I
80	arrived never appears; one sent after I arrived does"), not decomposable into independent resting
81	states without losing the claim.
82	
83	- A saga case is an ordered list of **steps**; each step = a caption plus an action against the
84	  fake world; after each step the runner captures one golden frame `<slug>.<id>.step-NN.png`.
85	- The **caption narrates the story** in user terms — captions surface in the gallery.
86	- One saga = one leaf; the frames are that one case's expected (all frames pixel-exact, same
87	  ownership rules as any golden). Keep sagas to 3–6 frames; a longer story is usually two sagas.
88	- Saga steps drive the **same real entry point** as every other kind (the shipped app shell/render
89	  function) — a saga must never become a scripted slideshow of hand-arranged states.
90	
91	**Animated saga goldens** (recording the motion, not the frames). A per-step frame proves a resting
92	state; a saga can instead be **one animated golden** — an APNG per leaf — recording the real UI
93	*moving* between steps. What keeps it delay-free and deterministic:
94	
95	- **Strip dead delay, keep the animation.** Render time is virtual, so a scripted wait is a run of
96	  *identical* frames — dedup consecutive identical frames and clamp any single hold, so the golden
97	  holds motion, never waiting (a 3 s wait must not become 3 s of golden).
98	- **Lossless, so byte-identity still holds.** Encode APNG, not GIF (whose palette and dithering
99	  aren't deterministic); the comparison stays exact byte-identity and a mismatch writes a per-frame
100	  `expected | actual | diff` to the gitignored failures dir. Capture at a low DPR — lossless costs
101	  no fidelity for it. Flutter reads each frame off the `RepaintBoundary` via `toImage` inside
102	  `runAsync` (the fake-async test zone won't otherwise complete the byte read).
103	- **Mark the gesture.** Paint an expanding ring at each real pointer gesture over the pre-reaction
104	  frame so the strip shows *where* the user acted; programmatic world changes draw none.
105	
106	## 5. Determinism or it isn't spec
107	
108	A rendered expected is only owner-ownable if it is byte-stable forever:
109	
110	- **Pin the clock.** One shared reference time (`REFERENCE_NOW`) threaded to everything that
111	  formats or compares dates; fixture data is authored relative to it. Never wall-clock.
112	- **Fake every nondeterministic input**: network (map tiles, avatars — deterministic generated
113	  substitutes), randomness, platform sensors, locale (pin it; date copy is locale-sensitive),
114	  viewport (one fixed logical size and pixel ratio).
115	- **Load real fonts** in the render harness — test environments default to a glyph-less stub that
116	  renders text as boxes. Load the product's bundled families plus the
117	  icon font; watch for styles that don't inherit the family (button text styles are the classic
118	  leak) — pin the family there explicitly.
119	- **Never wait for "settled".** Indeterminate spinners animate forever; use fixed-duration pumps
120	  so an in-flight state is a capturable, deterministic frame.
121	
122	## 6. Rendering recipes per stack
123	
124	- **Browser-extension / DOM products** (the origin recipe): feed the case's fake data to the real
125	  `render()` in a jsdom document seeded from the real HTML, fold the real CSS on as inline styles,
126	  rasterize with satori + resvg, compare with pixelmatch at **zero tolerated diff ratio**. No real
127	  browser: deterministic and dependency-light, at a documented fidelity tradeoff.
128	- **Flutter**: widget-test golden files are the native equivalent — pump the real app shell
129	  against the fake world and `matchesGoldenFile`; `--update-goldens` is the refresh lane. Load
130	  fonts from the FontManifest (icons included). The fake world (scripted location/auth/backend
131	  that also *records* what the UI asked) is the product's own testing library so the requirements
132	  package and unit tests share it.
133	- Whatever the stack: the comparison is **pixel-exact**. A tolerance is a standing invitation for
134	  unreviewed drift; if a platform renders unstably, fix the determinism (fonts, clock, fakes), not
135	  the threshold.
136	
137	## 7. The gallery is derived output
138	
139	- The spec doubles as a visual gallery: under every image-kind leaf, machine-managed image lines
140	  (tagged with an HTML comment marker) embed the committed goldens — saga leaves get their full
141	  captioned storyboard strip.
142	- A committed **gallery gate** keeps the doc equal to the generator's output byte-for-byte.
143	  Regenerate via the tool, never by hand.
144	
145	## 8. Refresh is a review step
146	
147	One committed refresh entry point regenerates all goldens **and** the gallery together, so they
148	cannot skew. Running it is how an *intended* UI change lands — the refreshed PNGs ride the diff
149	for the owner to approve. It is never how a red case gets fixed: the re-baselining approval
150	procedure (surface actual/expected/diff, ask, only then re-baseline) is canon in the
151	writing-tests skill and the spec-driven-product playbook.
